highlights.description: Initial release of systemspec-crypto: a Go-first, machine-readable IR describing the cryptography a system uses as facts and evidence, never prose. Implementations separate `capabilities` (what they can do) from `usedCapabilities` (what the system does with them), and every claim carries a verification state (discovered → inferred → review-required → verified → attested).
A `cryptospec` CLI validates a spec against structural rules and reports a human-readable summary; the same subcommands mount under a family aggregate CLI via `NewRootCommand`/`NewCommand`.
Dogfooded end to end on the public plexusone/omniagent platform (Argon2id passwords, SHA-256 token hashing, ECDSA/RSA JWT verification, crypto/rand CSPRNG), and exported to a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM.

added.description: Core IR types: Spec envelope with format-semver `specVersion`, system identity, and scope
Shared primitives: Lifecycle vocabulary, Provenance, and type-prefixed ID conventions

Implementation, Algorithm, and Use models — Implementation separates capabilities from usedCapabilities (the anti-hallucination control); Use ties an algorithm to a purpose, component, configuration, locations, and evidence
Evidence, Claim, and the Verification state machine; claims are the single verification surface, covering inventory objects by reference
Go-first JSON Schema generation pipeline (invopop/jsonschema), embedded via go:embed and linted clean by schemakit for static-type friendliness

Structural validation rules engine: referential integrity, capability containment, controlled-vocabulary conformance, ID conventions and uniqueness, and evidence requirements on verified/attested claims
`cryptospec validate` command with text and JSON output and error-gated exit codes
`cryptospec report` command: internal summary of implementations, algorithms, uses grouped by purpose, and claims by verification state
CycloneDX CBOM export bridge and `cryptospec cbom export` command; the lossy projection reports the facts CBOM cannot carry

fixed.description: Capability containment is enforced only when an implementation enumerates its capabilities, so a managed KMS/HSM may declare usage without listing its full capability set
